title: Move sessions out of process memory
summary: Sessions live in a `Map` inside each API process, so every deploy logs everyone out and the second replica can't see the first one's logins. Before I write the plan, I want to settle how the shared store should behave. **Round 2 has two questions** that follow from your first answers.
status: Round 2 of questions. No code changed yet.

blocks.title: Scope
blocks.question: Ship the shared store on its own, with the list of signed-in devices as a follow-up?
blocks.context: The store alone fixes the logouts. The device list adds a settings page and two endpoints.

options.label: Store now, device list later
options.summary: Smallest change that fixes the bug.

options.label: Both in this change
options.summary: One migration instead of two, but twice the review.

blocks.title: Session store
blocks.question: Keep sessions in a Postgres table?
blocks.context: We already run Postgres 15 (`src/db.ts`). Peak load is about 40 auth checks per second.

options.label: Postgres table
options.summary: No new infrastructure; one indexed read per request.
options.evidence: Spiked on a scratch branch: the read adds 1.1 ms at p95.

options.label: Redis
options.summary: Fastest, but a new service to deploy, monitor and back up.

blocks.title: What an auth check talks to
Expiry
blocks.question: Expire a session after 30 days without use?

options.label: 30 days, sliding
options.summary: What the in-memory sessions do today.

options.label: 30 days from login
options.summary: Simpler, but active users are signed out once a month.

blocks.title: Cutover
blocks.question: Accept that everyone is signed out once, when this deploys?
blocks.context: Today's sessions exist only in process memory, so there is nothing to copy into the table.

options.label: Yes, one logout
options.summary: Every deploy does this today anyway.

options.label: Read both stores for a release
options.summary: No logout, but the old Map stays for a release and needs sticky sessions meanwhile.

blocks.title: Sweeping expired sessions
blocks.question: Delete expired sessions hourly from the API, with a Postgres advisory lock so only one replica sweeps?
blocks.context: You asked for a 90-day cap on top of the 30-day sliding expiry, so a session ends at whichever comes first.

options.label: Hourly sweep in the API
options.summary: No new moving parts; the lock keeps replicas from racing.

options.label: pg_cron job
options.summary: Runs inside Postgres, but the extension isn't enabled in production.

options.label: Only check expiry on read
options.summary: No job at all, but the table grows without bound.
